integrity.fixed_point_basis: A mixed-radix one-parameter subgroup gives pairwise distinct tensor-coordinate weights, and every coordinate tensor has multilinear rank one in every mode.
integrity.object_basis: Landsberg--Weyman define subspace varieties by containment in tensor products of bounded-dimensional factor subspaces; Yang identifies these loci with bounded mode-flattening ranks.
integrity.primary_slot_basis: The arXiv metadata for math/0601452 lists Algebraic Geometry first and MSC 14Q15 among the paper's classification codes; the paper devotes a full section to subspace varieties.
integrity.stratum_basis: Exact multilinear-rank loci are finite intersections of matrix-rank equalities and inequalities, hence constructible; cumulative Euler constancy and additivity force all higher exact strata to vanish.

scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to ordinary higher-order subspace varieties defined by mode-flattening rank bounds.
Exact multilinear-rank strata use compactly supported Euler characteristic because they are quasi-projective.
The two-factor matrix specialization is prior coverage and is excluded from the higher-order novelty claim.
The localization argument is short, so an unindexed folklore observation remains possible.
title: Euler characteristic collapses the entire multilinear-rank filtration
